newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki unfazed by jitters, powers to new high.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki unfazed by jitters, powers to new high.

text.p: Finnish shares defied a jolt to European markets from strong U.S. jobs data on Friday to take the index to another record close in massive almost one billion markka volume with lively Nokia ending strong.
After spending most of the day in positive ground, the HEX slipped late on the U.S. payrolls report, but sprang back partly on short-covering to close up 0.36 percent at 2,623.4 points.

Bourse engine Nokia ended up 4.50 markka at 297.00 after touching a 15-month high of 302.10 early on after what analysts called an "encouraging" fourth-quarter earnings report from Motorola, its U.S. rival in mobile phones.
Nokia accounted for a third of total volume, which was spread among a wide range of shares, brokers said.
Foods and animal feeds group Raisio closed up 10.00 markka at 320.00 markka but was off an intrasession high of 322.00, but still at its highest levels since early September last year.
Raisio made up seven percent of total volume with heavy buying by international investors, brokers said. They could give no specific reason for why the sudden focus on the share.
Forestry stocks failed to hold early gains and the index fell 0.72 percent. UPM-Kymmene fell 0.90 to end at 98.20 markka.
Hardware group Starckjohann exceptionally became the second most traded company as SKOPBank sold 21 million shares for about seven markka each. The share closed down 0.60 at 7.10 markka.
Insurer Pohjola rose in hefty volume to close up 7.00 markka at 115.00, tracking recent gains in Sampo brokers said.
